correctness.rationale: Renewal equation with the Laplace success probability gives the exact mean for every positive parameter choice. The reciprocal success probability is a polynomial with strictly positive elementary-symmetric coefficients, yielding strict convexity for n>=2 and decreasing behavior for n=1. A positive-rate added stage contributes an increasing polynomial, so its new optimum is strictly smaller. Equal-stage minimizers solve a strictly decreasing root equation and converge to the stated unique Lambert-branch constant. An independent transient-state linear-system checker passed 2006 exact-rational assertions on n<=5; finite checks supplement, not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Dynamic landscapes can create temporary dispersal bridges. In an explicit nontrivial ecological crossing mechanism, stationary bridge availability does not determine colonization speed: increasing turnover improves mean crossing from a closed start only until a unique finite speed when at least two stages are needed. The exact two-stage onset, all-heterogeneous-stage ordering, and length-dependent 1/n scaling form a complete useful benchmark for transit-time effects, not a trivial one-parameter restatement or an arbitrary slice. It does not purport to calibrate a field policy.
